channel.description: Latest articles from Her View From Home (herviewfromhome.com)

item.title: To the woman who just found out she's been living a lie with her husband
item.description: A letter of support to a woman who's just found out her husband has not upheld his marriage vows. God will not leave you.

item.title: Why my son is missing from our family photo
item.description: My son with autism is a teenager now and he can tell us when things are too much for him and we are confident enough to listen.

item.title: Ours is a love that still chooses
item.description: Our love is not flashy and new, but this married life as husband and wife produces devotion that still chooses each other.

item.title: I Love the Man Behind the Beard - Her View From Home
item.description: I love my husband's beard and how it has come in and out of our lives throughout the years, and I love him even more.

item.title: I'm a teacher but it's not my whole life
item.description: You may think I'm a "bad teacher" because I leave my work life at work and focus on my home life at home, but it's how I need to be.

item.title: Midlife is this space between arrivals and departures
item.description: I stood in the airport. Outside the window was the plane that would take me home—a place and a scene I’d been in many times in the past 20 years. Yet there’s something different here in the middle of life. We write about the beginning of life with babies and small children, and the end of life when we say goodbye at one’s passing, but why aren’t we writing more about the middle? item.title: The silent strength of a working mom
item.description: The working mom does so much in both her home and at her job, and God goes before her in everything she carries.

item.title: My husband is proof good fathers exist
item.description: I know good fathers are out there because I married a man who became one, even though my own dad was not there for me.

item.title: When your mom is a funeral director, you learn about loss—and love
item.description: In my work as a funeral director, I want my kids to see that grief is not something to be afraid of, but to be held gently.

item.title: We may have sold the car, but I'll never part with the memories
item.description: We finally sold the car I drove for years as my kids grew and even though it's fun to have something new, I'll never forget the memories.
